correctness.rationale: The weak-Carmichael criterion reduces 3^a p q to two divisibilities. The substitution d=p-1 and k=(3^a p-1)/(q-1) gives an exact bijective divisor parametrization and explicit finite bounds. The a=2 case is reduced to twelve displayed integer candidates, with exactly two prime pairs. Independent exact-integer enumeration agrees with the parametrization for a=1 through 5.

originality.rationale: The 2013 source discusses the 3^2 p_2...p_s family and lists 13833 and 321201, but also contains an internally inconsistent empty-intersection computation for the 9pq slice. The 2026 manuscript, OEIS, synonymous searches under weak/pseudo/generalized Carmichael terminology, and the current SCOPE archive did not reveal the stated all-a finite parametrization or cutoff-free 9pq classification. Originality remains to the best of our knowledge, with residual risk from older pseudo-Carmichael literature.

value.rationale: The theorem converts an infinite fixed-exponent search into a finite divisor computation with explicit bounds, globally classifies the 9pq slice, resolves a concrete literature discrepancy, and gives exact periodic lifting of any fixed prime pair across exponents.
